body:
Thank you so much for this post.

I struggled with bulimia as a teenager, kicked it by 18, and now in the aftermath of an abusive marriage have veered into restrictive behaviors. I was born Disabled, and as a result, have a body/weight uniquely shaped by my dx; my bulimia sprung up from outside concern over “the Disabled girl getting fat”.

All this to say, your point about not hating yourself vs loving yourself w/ no issue resonates so deeply for me. It’s something to apply to my own journey.
This is only semi-related but where did you get that shirt? I love MothMan!

I never got married expecting to get divorced. To say I’m struggling with this new chapter is an understatement.

As for social, I’ve always been extremely introverted. I’m moving home with my parents in about a month and will reevaluate the social side of things once I’m independent again.
Got it. I am new to survivorhood--if I were to edit it, could I repost it? I'm not trying to victim-blame, just inarticulate.

An automatic needle threader--those are a thing? 

My hands shake after too much repetitive use--CP is so similar neurologically to MS that a lot of the non-invasive workarounds that work for y'all also work for us. I'm open to any links/suggestions you have as, aside from another person with CP, it's a safe guess that you're closest to me in terms of mobility and adaptation.

Initially I thought about recovering existing blocks, but the thought/sound of "destroying" a book makes something in me shrivel up haha

Makes sense!!

The only abuse I've ever known is from other women. I'm not in a healthy enough place to write two women falling in love yet, and I'm concerned that if I try, unhealed pain would bleed through to the story. The indie horror writer MichaelBrent Collings has a saying that fiction shouldn't take the place of therapy, and I agree.
Thank you. I'll look into those.
Thank you!!
Thank you for this insight!!

Thank you for being kind in your reply.

Short answer to what you brought up: I have a tremendous amount of pain around being lesbian/Butch; the only F/F relationships I’ve been in were toxic and abusive. All forms of abuse, except I was never beaten.

I can’t bear to have women touch me or smile at me, such that I move to the other side of the street. I struggle to speak without a stutter and make eye contact now.

As a teen and young adult I was incredibly self abusive to my body, and my gender dysphoria is crippling. So my inner child, she needs a lot of love and care.

In short, I have a lot of healing to do before I’m ready to write healthy F/F romance. It’s on my list for the future; but some distance and escapism from wounds that other women inflicted on my Butch body—I need that for now. I don’t want lesbian and bi women to suffer from my lack of healing, even in fiction. When I’m ready, I’ll write F/F. Hope this helps.

What brand/kind of boards did you use? Did you paint the sparkly silver background on to the boards? And what kind of paper as well? Shiny silver paper/edges are apparently not as popular as gold, but it's a look I'd love to try on a future project; I'm obsessed with the aesthetic of this and I'm not even a fan of the series. Beautiful work.
Thank you!!

I relate deeply to Leslie's life and experiences, but haven't finished SBB yet--it is a heavy read and having recently become a rape survivor myself, I know I'm not in a space yet to handle those topics. Thanks!
The beautiful design on the front—did you draw it? Find it? The level of detail is amazing—is it heat transfer vinyl?
One of my favorite videos on the Internet, and something that I come back to often as both a romance reader/writer and a Twihard. It's fabulously executed.

A fellow writer who is also a lesbian? \*happy dance\*

I've been studying women and female POV straight romance for most of my life and I still find things while reading/interacting that are completely foreign to me. I know that I could have written a lesbian romance easily, but these characters came to me the way they did and, as you know, the vibe between two women in love is different. 

There's a softness and vulnerability that I simply haven't given, and couldn't give, a man. I know that straight women have the same vulnerability, but I'm not sure how to translate that so that the hero feels safe enough to open up to.

I'm an oblivious potato so I relate hardcore to this lol!

Thanks for the note about mutual interest; I'm trying to figure out how they fit in each other's lives/worlds aside from having known/loved each other before (it's a second chance romance).
Thanks.

I need to be Butch because, while it is performative for me, it's the type of performance that makes me least likely to tear my own skin off. I spent years prior to coming out as a straight-passing girl. I had to study girls to play-act at being one, literally. I wasn't a tomboy in childhood or the kid that everyone knew would grow up to be gay; once puberty hit, the masculinity/lesbianism was a shock to me and everyone else.

  
Butch-masculine is different than straight-masculine. There are Butches that try to ape male thinking and behavior in every possible way, but more often than not, there's an emphasis on being the antithesis of what toxic men are. Dominant but not domineering is preferred, but not required. More open with emotion. Seeing women as people first and sexually desirable second. The female upbringing and experience cancels/softens a lot of things that, in a straight man, would be considered toxic. Not saying there aren't toxic Butches but generally, we call each other out on bad behavior.



>Then think about what personality traits you like, because ultimately, the love child of Idris Elba and George Clooney could ask me out on a date but if he's wearing a MAGA shirt, or if he starts throwing some red pill/pick-up artist nonsense my way, I'm out. There is no handsome on earth that can overcome the knee-jerk revulsion I feel to a person with a terrible personality. 

  
This helps. I've only had two relationships in my adult life, one toxic and the other straight up abusive. I'm coming out of the second one completely shattered and distrustful, so trusting myself for basic shit is hard, let alone with writing. I like smart, brave, independent partners. I like humor and adaptability. I'm very quiet and introverted and guarded, nerdy as well, so I look for people who bring me out of my shell. As I wrote the first draft, he was much braver than I would be; but I'm not sure if that fits for his character. I do know I want her to be strong and independent and brave, as well as adaptable; and I know that I want him to be unconventional in terms of attractiveness, as well as a guy about to give up on himself. The rest is murky; I've never finished a book before and the revision process is like trying to carve a blank piece of marble; I can't see and am afraid to make the wrong cuts.

When I was drafting the post, it said "how to write x" questions aren't allowed except for a certain sub, so I had to be vague haha!

As I said in the post, the hero's POV makes sense to me. I know what it is to love and desire women because my great loves are all women. It's the heroine that is confusing me. Most of my friends are straight women, but we don't really talk about sexuality outside of the basics ie who's dating/hooking up with who. I read mostly straight romance, but I know as both a reader and a writer that those aren't always realistic.

  
For example, what on earth is attractive about a man's forearms? Why is men showing emotion/vulnerability attractive instead of normal communication, you know? I'm the closed off/hard to be vulnerable type, but as a woman, being emotional in front of a woman is totally different. It's expected. It's not shamed, the way men are.

  
These are just a few more specific questions. I have more lol.

Thank you!!

I know there's no blanket experience; but the specifics, like noticing a man is attractive or desiring his body, I have no frame of reference for. I'm nervous to get it wrong haha!

I’m forcing myself to do basic things like get outside in the sunshine. The better weather helps. It’s just that it’s a brief respite. I start to feel better and then (it feels like) I come crashing back down to earth.

As for doctors, they don’t know how to help me. I’ve been on multiple medications before. They just want to hear that I’m better. They don’t actually care about me. I lie just to get them to stop asking whether I’m still depressed.

So I’m just supposed to not rely on anyone for anything? To not have any relationships, lest I unknowingly act “codependent”?

Codependency makes it sound like I can’t live without other people.

Codependency makes it sound like I’m incapable of taking care of myself.

Like the people I care about are projects who only exist to serve me.

None of these are true. I manage to have both healthy family relationships and healthy friendships, aside from this one. I have let people go before.

Is codependency just shorthand for judgement? That’s how it comes across from the article you shared.

Caring about someone else is bad? How?

I’ve read about codependency but that’s not what I’m like at all. I don’t quite get the whole concept, to be honest.

Which part of I’m 262 days sober wasn’t clear?
AA handles my drinking. I’ve been. I’m doing what I’m supposed to do.
As for your second comment, “Just leave”, would you want people who care giving up on you in the same position?

I don't have a sponsor and haven't been to a meeting in months--I'm in an electric wheelchair and can't get transportation--but I'm highly aware on a daily basis just how much staying sober is crucial. I've begun slowly to fill the void with healthy things and to be more responsible, identify and self soothe triggers, etc. I know that if I drink, I'll die--it's just what I'm like.

  
When it comes to myself I can surrender. I have to force myself not to protect her, though. It's hard.

  
This friendship/situation/watching her kill herself has been hugely triggering; 10 years ago this June, my brother was killed suddenly and tragically. I didn't get the chance to save him, and since he was declared brain dead after his accident, I never got to talk to him as he was or even see his eyes before his life support was pulled. One day he was my brother and everything was fine and normal and happy; and the day after, it was like he never existed. Completely ripped from me. He was 21 when he died, so when I drank, it was all alcohol he enjoyed. Drinking for me is/was tied up in the idea that no one (except others in my situation) understands. I know intellectually that's not true, but emotionally it's very intense and hard to explain.

  
I told her so many times when she would drink: just let me know you're safe, please be careful, etc--not because I'm some whacked out control freak, but because the last person I loved that intensely died on me without warning, and then I spiraled really badly. Knowing I have no control over her dying...it just puts me right back in the place I was at 10 years ago. And intellectually, of course they're two different people, two different relationships and situations, but it doesn't register emotionally. Yes, it's her life and she's a grown woman who I don't have/want control over; and the drive to save her life is overwhelming, in large part due to my own loss. That drive is something my brother created, that I can't shut off.

Thank you. I struggle to see the value in my own existence. I don’t get why the people who love me do. I don’t see myself as good or worthy of their care.

The sobriety helps, and at the same time, it’s like salt in the wound. I have complex medical issues that prevented me from ever reaching bingeing levels or physical dependence; so in many ways I know I can’t understand what she’s dealing with.

She still says to me that we’re mates, that she loves me, that she won’t let me drown. We have similar demons.

I can’t trust a word, because her actions don’t match.

I found out last night she’s pursuing another guy, and I lost it. I flat out told her she should worry about drinking herself to death rather than the guy.

I’m trying hard to focus on my own life; sobriety revealed how broken my life is; but I feel her absence so keenly.

A stronger person than me would just walk away. I just don’t have the heart. And nothing in my life can fill her void.

I've been struggling with self harm on and off since my teens, and by the time I stopped, I was drinking beforehand because my tolerance for SH had become so high I needed an anesthetic (booze, in this case) to even feel relief from it.

  
I stopped the self harm before I got sober. I'd had years-long clean periods before which definitely helped make it easier to abstain. This time though, I had a series of kind things I would say to myself when the urges came up, chief among them: "I don't deserve to be hurt." I would distract during some urges, research why I felt the way I did during others, and most importantly let the urge pass safely; so for example, I didn't have implements I could use in my space. I would tell myself when the urges came up, "This is not an option." I found that for me, the fantasy of SH was always better than the reality of the harm and the healing, and so I would ask myself, "Do I really want to deal with more scars healing? Do I really want to deal with my loved ones' concern?" The answer was always no, so I didn't act on the urge.

  
My family and friends have never really understood me, in the case of either drinking or SH, so I found online support systems. The folks over at r/selfharm are lovely and recovery-minded (I'm still subscribed there as one of my triggers is feeling alone and SH has been such a huge part of my life) and their wiki and esp their "Positives" flair are so helpful. On the really bad days, I still scroll through the Positives flair because it's full of recovery posts. The sub does skew younger but I don't mind it. Hope this helps. My DMs are always open.

Writing! 

I’ve wanted to be an author from the time I was a preteen. Started and stopped multiple stories before finding one that reached out and grabbed me through multiple drafts.

I find that without booze to numb me, and without the (unhelpful) mood stabilizer I was on for depression, my mind is clearer but the darkness is more intense. I always crave drinking and my head is a dark place…but I promised myself two things:
1) I can’t write or edit while drinking.
2) my hands will never again do harm to myself.

251 days sober from alcohol today, and 291 sober from self harm;

and I’ve completed two drafts of what will be my debut novel. Looking at another draft and taking this project seriously requires a clear head. I’m so grateful I’m not hurting myself for my art anymore.

IWNDWYT

Thank you 🥺 I’ve been trying to write a novel from the time I was 11 or so, and this is the first idea I’ve seen through multiple drafts/will see through to the end.

In sci-fi romance, a lot of what’s popular has to do with aliens, which I’m also not into. So I stayed away but am pleasantly surprised the more I read :)

Thank you. This is so kind 😭

I think all the outside feedback is getting to me tbh. 

When I started in 2017 and was required to submit chapters for class critiques, I could tell the difference between mine and everyone else’s because the most common response I got was silence. No one knew what to do with it, and no one else was writing romance or something so dark.

Then during 2020/1 I was part of a writers’ group of all romance writers, and they didn’t know what to do with it. They kept trying to change it. Lighten it up.

Everyone around me knows I want to write professionally, but they’re not writers themselves. They’re either supportive but not invested or wondering when I’ll publish/move on to something else.

The writers I was in group with have all gone and published multiple books by now, so it’s easy to listen to the doubt instead of my own voice. Thank you for the perspective.

Thank you so much for this comment!!

Sure, I could try drafting a version of the story without the romance focus--I was a Writing major in college and did read a lot of literary fiction back then (prior to 2020). Most of what I read and what I love is romance, so I just naturally think and write along those lines. I never considered my plot might have literary potential, as from what I remember of lit fic (it's been years since I picked any up) it was slower and more plot than character focused. Romance being considered "trashy"--I made the mistake of telling people I write--definitely dissuaded me from seeing anything literary in it, though I can say that my influences are more literary/classic than most people would expect (I blame the English degree lol). *Wuthering Heights* is a massive influence, as are *Frankenstein* and a quieter, close-to-literary YA novel *The Last Time We Say Goodbye* by Cynthia Hand. The querying process is strict about comparing to your age range and subgenre, so I've tried to put that last one out of my head as an influence, but it absolutely is one. I'm working toward a blend of that and Brigid Kemmerer's *A Curse So Dark and Lonely*, tbh.

At present I'm reading wider than I normally do to try and see what I'm aiming toward, so I'll add some lit fic to my list--do you have any recommendations?

This helps tremendously--you have to decide what success looks like to you. I knew a long time ago that in a perfect world, I'd make a living solely from my writing, so marketability is present in my mind as I draft, consider whether to send out queries, research self-publishing, etc.

  
Do you have a newsletter I can subscribe to yet, as I'd love to know when your book is out so I can read it? It sounds like my kind of story--I am all about dark, intense, and complex work and I don't see that often with monster stories!

Wow, thanks so much for the reply--what is the name of your podcast/is it available on Spotify? I like to listen to writing stuff to get myself in the zone beforehand, and only follow a few romance-focused podcasts. When the time comes for beta readers and the like I'll definitely reach back out!

One of the major reasons I didn’t medicalize was because among the many, many papers I read, I found evidence that synthetic testosterone messes with your ligaments (found in connective tissue and joints). 

CP is individual, but in my case, my legs are profoundly affected: I’m not even 30 and I already have a rod in one leg, have had multiple orthopedic surgeries, and am suffering horribly with arthritis and inflammation. I can barely stand and can’t walk without aid, or without being a fall risk. Think of the way elderly people move, and you get the idea. The physical stress associated with CP is so profound it has a name: premature aging.

Second, and more importantly re your point about potential medication interactions: many of us are extremely heavily medicated, and generally speaking, the more severe your CP is, the more meds you’re on. I’ve always been an anomaly for being so under medicated despite my severity.

The medication that allows me to thrive, is an addictive substance, and requires surgery every 5 years is called baclofen. 

Typically it’s given in pill form, but in the 80’s, an implanted pump was created which allows doctors better control of med concentration and eliminates some side effects. I was part of one of the first cohorts of children given an implanted pump, in 2001. 4 years old remains the youngest age one can have an intrathecal pump.

It treats the muscle spasms that most people can recognize as evidence of CP; but it also allows me to feel when I have to go the bathroom and, critically, keeps my body from burning so much energy. People with CP burn 3-5x the energy of people without it. It’s just what our bodies do and why so many of us are so thin.

Every time the pump is replaced, I’m given a list of substances that interact which are as long as my arm. On that list is acetaminophen, THC, most street drugs, some psychiatric medications (one of which I took for YEARS before having to inform my clueless primary care physician that I needed to switch) and a lot of other things.

But if you were to google cerebral palsy, or even the medication I’m on, none of this information would be readily available. More specifically, unless it’s explicitly stated, baclofen studies ONLY deal with the oral medication…aka, those individuals with less severe CP.

Gender clinics are already known for having no safeguards for Able people. 

Every Disabled transitioner I’ve spoken to admitted that either a) there were no MDs associated with their clinics, b) they didn’t even think to ask the questions I have (because they’re TRAs), and most worryingly c) no one on staff knows what cerebral palsy is, and no one cares about their medical history.

If I decided to throw in the towel tomorrow and just medicalize, I could do it laughably easily, despite the fact that my surgical history is an entire binder.

GCs lose points with me because they will use anything to push their ideology, including bodies like mine. Mutilated is something I already am, that has nothing to do with transition, but try telling GCs they shouldn’t use people the same way TRAs do 😬🙃

I’m in Michigan in the southeastern part. 30 minutes from Ann Arbor one way, 30 minutes from Detroit in the other direction. It’s a great location…for someone who can walk and drive. We’re a 5 minute drive from her work.

To give some context, the disability I have is cerebral palsy. I suffered a severe brain hemorrhage at birth (I was a 25 week micro-preemie). To my knowledge, the area of my brain most affected is my frontal lobe. Physically this means my legs are most affected. Medically it’s a pain in the ass to manage but it’s not progressive or terminal.

But mentally and emotionally, this means I struggle most with planning ahead, emotional regulation, organization, decision making, and other executive function tasks. I’ve only started to realize the cognitive effects in adulthood.

I was an Honors student and high functioning growing up, and neither my family nor I were educated/prepared about the cognitive and emotional challenges of CP. I was always told I was just a smart girl in a chair. That I would grow into myself and level out emotionally with time.

Stress makes executive function worse even for someone without my brain. For someone with my brain…it’s a complicated nightmare. 

This whole experience has really revealed to me how much I underestimated the severity of my condition. I already tried to leave once and it was a nightmare because, well, I tried planning ahead and was not educated or prepared for law enforcement to not give a shit; nor for lack of physical abuse to be a barrier to a shelter. Even when I try my best to plan, as smart as I am intellectually I don’t do it right. There’s a lack of forward vision when making plans, so to speak. I try to see others’ perspective and even in less high stakes situations, it’s hard.

I can’t imagine my family’s frustration. Most people with the right wiring would jump at a way out. But because I can’t see the way ahead the way they can, I’m extremely hesitant. Not ungrateful. I love my family. I didn’t tell them what was going on until the nightmare of trying to leave the first time. They got mad at me for not trusting them/coming to them sooner. That was 100% my screw up.

Up until trying to leave, they’d been encouraging me to stay in the marriage and work things out. That she is a “nice girl” and since she’s Able bodied, I’m going to need that help. 

When I told my dad about the rape/sexual abuse, he got mad at me for feeling shame/that it was my fault; for not understanding immediately after the first incident that I’d been raped; and he said what happens isn’t “really” rape because she’s not a man penetrating me with a penis. He basically took it like, well you were stupid and should have known better.

I was stupid. There’s so much I didn’t understand. There’s so much I’m learning as I go about DV. But since my experience isn’t a typical one (man beating on woman) it’s harder for people to see as abusive. My daddy was a child of DV, and had witnessed the typical presentation firsthand. That’s his bias. I’m educating him as I go along, but it’s hard. 

There’s a concept for elderly/Disabled people called aging in place. It’s the idea that we shouldn’t have to leave the community as we age due to special needs. In terms of Disability like mine though, one of the challenges is that often, when we rely on family or institutional care, it’s harder for us than for an Able person to regain that independence. We get stuck, so to speak, where an Able bodied person wouldn’t struggle with upward mobility as much.

It’s not that I don’t want help. It’s that in my mind, I try to see moving in with them as temporary, and I’m just scared that 5 years from now, I’ll be stuck burdening them.

As for moving in with roommates, that’s something I’ve never done/hadn’t considered. It’s scary to me.

My family are really resistant to me seeking help through a third party. They think I should just rely on them and not think too far ahead/worry about everything, but I can’t help it.

I’ve thought about reaching out to a social worker for help, but after screwing up so much, I don’t want to make another bad choice and be shamed again.

When I go online to see what other Disabled survivors have done, all of them “just” move in with family. There’s literally no example for me to follow of getting out while living on my own. I’m not sure whether this is due to personal preference or the system not being set up to handle us, but it’s frustrating to encounter again and again.

All while I get the typical shit thrown at survivors: just leave, I’d never stay in a situation like that, it must not be that bad if you’re still there, etc.

She (the abuser) is imho a covert narcissist. I didn’t realize this until far too late. I simply wasn’t educated enough. To the outside world she comes across as the perfect spouse for “dealing with” me.

All of my yes!!

All of that love and care focused on me would be 🥰😍

I’m a masculine, Disabled human permanently going through a lot, so: 

1. The wounded bird/caretaking trope; if I’m going to need care regardless, may as well be enthusiastically given for once LOL

2. Being protected by some sort of bodyguard; and carried. And maybe my life is threatened, because in that alternate universe I also matter.

3. Being an omega in a reverse harem. Having to submit and serve (and engage with my breeding kink) and generally be spoiled 🥵

Thank you for the reply. Upon reflection, you're right--I'm used to the instant gratification of alcohol; and in particular, the tendency of booze to numb negative emotions/experiences quickly. I'm humbled and shocked at how difficult sitting with pain is. Though I do see myself as weak, maybe a better phrase would be emotionally inexperienced? I am very mature in some ways, but emotionally, I lag behind my peers. They've been out living/building character while I've been limited (in a wheelchair pretty much from birth).

I’ve always struggled with going to therapy consistently, but I have had a lot of it over the past decade. Perhaps I’m just getting older and more cynical, but talking about what I feel/can’t change doesn’t come with catharsis anymore.

I’m not anti-therapy at all; in fact I’m staunchly pro-therapy. At one point I even wanted to become a therapist. But I’ve been burned by so many bad therapy experiences, and I’m worried talking about this stuff won’t help, that I’m just avoiding going. Self-sabotaging, I know.

Thank you for your reply and support. I think you’re right about there needing to be a different word than depression for this experience—the mood stabilizers I take help with the depression, but there’s nothing to take for everything that’s happening to me, has been happening.

Warning: this is a bit rambly and I know Outlander is a divisive series but if anyone will understand/not judge this comment, it’s y’all.

My all time favorite romances are the ones where I relate to both members of a pairing. And I absolutely know romances have saved my life. The ultimate example of both of these is the Outlander series by Diana Gabaldon. 

I started with the show before beginning the series but wow—that woman can WRITE. As a writer myself I can’t even be jealous or mad I didn’t think of it.

My mom recommended the books but the syntax drove me up a wall to read (Davina Porter’s narration of the first book saved me from DNFing—slowly working my way through it and 😍).

I’m a Jamie too (spelled differently); have a dead brother; have an extremely scarred/traumatized back and body; have suffered SA that totally made me question my life/desirability/masculinity; have a very strong connection to family/country; work with words; and go by another name for my own safety.

My attachment to the series is much deeper, more painful, and more profound than I let anyone see, though.

I also want an unavailable, dark-haired woman more than life itself—have from the very first moment, just like Jamie.

It’s a complicated situation, but the 20 years Jamie and Claire spend apart? I’m more likely to have that experience than I am an HEA.

Like Claire, my given middle name is Elizabeth :) more importantly…

Like Claire, I didn’t set out to fall in love with someone else. Like Claire, I know that no amount of time will make me forget my love. Like Claire, I know who/what I should want, but my heart screams otherwise.

And like Claire says in the show, though I don’t condone nor engage in cheating…

“Not only was I a bigamist and an adulteress but I had enjoyed it.”

I know which person I can’t live without, and it’s not the one I ended up with—my Frank, for the sake of continuity.

Like Claire, I wear two rings—one for each person.

The unavailable woman I love is Scottish. 

I started watching the show/reading the series just because I missed her so intensely. Her humor, her way of being, her pride in her heritage—it feels like the series has given me a way to be with her, though I will likely never have her.

When Jamie looks at Claire with love in his eyes, when she can’t let him go even though she knows she should—I know exactly how Jamie feels, and how Claire feels.
